analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch (head hunk at lines 1030-1048) adds a paragraph describing PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, a new prompt-token reuse cache. It reuses token IDs of pieces seen earlier in the same prefix-cache scope, encodes new long prompts on up to four cores, uses ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates, runs sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on a mismatch, and can be turned off with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0. I reviewed the supplied units, which are the base excerpt (lines 2008-2248, unchanged Flint and Bonsai text) and the head excerpt (lines 1-415). Neither contains the added hunk text, so I could only evaluate it from the patch excerpt. No code, config, or control changes are present in the supplied evidence, and no threat-model control is weakened by the documentation itself.

Open question for code-level review: the doc says the cache reuses token IDs only within one cache scope and never crosses scopes. That is the same property the T-041 mitigations rely on for account isolation (coordinator-authored cacheSalt). If PromptTokenCache is in-memory and keyed per scope, it could form a new cross-tenant timing channel (TTFT or tokenization latency) or retain prompt-derived data (A-001) in provider memory. The source change is not supplied, so I cannot confirm the scope keying, the memory bounds, the lifetime or eviction, or whether it honours the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. I raise this as a review question, not a finding, because there is no evidence of a regression. The next pass should examine PromptTokenCache.swift and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for scope keying, a cache key that cannot be attacker-chosen, bounded growth, and token-ID equivalence with the unchanged applyChatTemplate path. T-041 may also need a note if this cache adds a same-account oracle.
